title: App Registration Audit: UR - App - SII 2.0

credentials.note: App relies entirely on client secrets. No OIDC/federated identity is configured.

microsoft_graph.risk_reason: Contains Application.ReadWrite.All + AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All + Directory.ReadWrite.All. This is effectively full administrative access to Entra ID.

rights_management.risk_reason: Permission to access Microsoft Rights Management Service

azure_active_directory_graph.risk_reason: Legacy Azure AD Graph API permissions, should migrate to Microsoft Graph equivalents

assignments.description: para poder hacer release desde Azure DevOps
assignments.risk_reason: Contributor at subscription level grants write access to ALL Resource Groups, including shared infrastructure. Far exceeds the minimum needed for Web App deployment.

oidc_federated_credential_proposal.subject: repo:FREDYASARMIENTOT/HERMES-ENTERPRISE:environment:production
oidc_federated_credential_proposal.note: NOT created. This is a proposal only.

compatibility_with_hermes.minimumPermissionNeeded: Website Contributor on specific Web App or Contributor on specific Resource Group (not subscription-wide)
compatibility_with_hermes.humanEntraRoleNeeded: Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator — subscription Contributor is NOT sufficient to manage federated credentials

verdict.reason: UR - App - SII 2.0 is an institutional application with CRITICAL permissions: (1) Subscription-wide Contributor (not scoped to a specific RG), (2) Application.ReadWrite.All + Directory.ReadWrite.All + AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All in Microsoft Graph. Reusing this for Hermes would: (a) expose SII 2.0 operations to any compromise in the GitHub Actions pipeline, (b) grant GitHub more permissions than needed for Web App deployment, (c) violate the principle of least privilege. A new, dedicated App Registration with scoped permissions is the correct approach.
verdict.recommendation: Create a NEW App Registration 'Hermes-Enterprise-OIDC' with: Contributor on RG-Hermes-Proyectos only (not subscription), NO Microsoft Graph API permissions (OIDC federated credential login does not require Graph), Website Contributor on specific Web Apps if needed.
risks: Subscription-wide Contributor — Hermes would inherit ability to modify ALL Azure resources
Directory.ReadWrite.All — could read/write all Entra ID directory data
Application.ReadWrite.All — could modify/delete other App Registrations
AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All — could grant itself or others any permission
No federated credentials means secrets must be managed, rotated, and stored
human_entra_admin_required: Configuring federated credentials on the new App Registration
Consenting to API permissions (if any) on the new App Registration
Note: Subscription-level Contributor is NOT sufficient for these operations

questions_answered.1_can_we_reuse: NO — DO_NOT_REUSE. Excessive permissions risk SII 2.0 operations.
questions_answered.3_current_permissions: Subscription Contributor + 10 Microsoft Graph application roles + 17 delegated scopes + legacy AD Graph permissions
questions_answered.4_minimum_needed: Contributor on RG-Hermes-Proyectos (not subscription) + no Graph permissions needed for OIDC deploy
questions_answered.5_entra_admin_needed: Create new App Registration + federated credential — requires Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator role in Entra ID
questions_answered.7_can_github_deploy_without_shared_infra: Yes, if scoped to RG-Hermes-Proyectos Contributor only (not subscription-wide)
questions_answered.8_verdict: DO_NOT_REUSE — new dedicated App Registration required
